channel.title: Lincoln recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Ford Explorer, Lincoln Aviator Seats May Recline
item.description: Some Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles have a driver's seat that may recline on its own when no one is sitting in it, such as when the vehicle is remotely unlocked or remotely started. If the seat back moves unexpectedly, it could trap a person sitting in the second row.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Second-Row Seats May Shift Unexpectedly
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles because the switch for the easy-entry second-row outer seats may bind or stick. This can cause the seat to unlatch, tip, or slide unexpectedly. A seat that moves unexpectedly may not properly restrain a passenger in a crash. This is a phased recall — the repair will become available at different times depending on the model and model year. Dealers will inspect and replace the switch bezel as necessary, at no cost.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln SUVs: Transmission Park System May Fail
item.description: On affected vehicles, a part called the park pawl, which is supposed to lock the transmission in place when you put the vehicle in park, may engage while the vehicle is still moving. This can damage the park system, the mechanism that normally keeps the vehicle from rolling once it has been shifted into park.

item.title: Ford Mustang, Lincoln Nautilus, Navigator Instrument Cluster Blank
item.description: Ford is recalling certain 2019 Mustang, Nautilus, and Navigator vehicles because an earlier repair for this same problem did not fully fix it. When the vehicle is started, the instrument panel display may fail to work and show a blank screen instead of turning on. This means the gauges and warning lights on the dashboard may not be visible to the driver.

item.title: Lincoln Nautilus Lane Assist May Miss Hands-Off Alert
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Lincoln Nautilus vehicles because an earlier repair for this problem did not fully fix it. The lane center assist system may fail to properly detect when a driver has taken their hands off the steering wheel for a prolonged period. Because of this, the system may not give the driver the intended warning telling them to put their hands back on the wheel.

item.title: Ford Expedition, Lincoln Navigator Seat Belt May Lock
item.description: Certain Ford Expedition and Lincoln Navigator vehicles have a problem with the seat belt pretensioner in the driver's seat, the front passenger seat, or both. The pretensioner may inadvertently lock the seat belt, which then will not retract or extend the way it normally should.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Windshield Wiper Arms May Break
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Expedition, F-250 SD, F-350 SD, F-450 SD, F-550 SD, F-600 SD, and Lincoln Navigator vehicles because the windshield wiper arms may break. When a wiper arm breaks, the windshield wipers can fail to work properly, which can make it harder for the driver to see the road ahead. Dealers will inspect the wiper arms on affected vehicles and replace them if necessary, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ford Explorer and Lincoln Models Camera and ADAS Loss
item.description: In these Ford Explorer and Lincoln vehicles, a part called the Image Processing Module A may unexpectedly reset itself multiple times. When this module resets, it can cause the vehicle to lose the rearview camera image. It can also cause the vehicle to lose several driver assistance features at the same time, including pre-collision assist, lane-keeping assist, and blind-spot monitoring.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Seat Belt Anchor Bolts May Loosen
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles because the seat belt anchor bolts at the second-row outer seating positions may not be properly secured. A loose seat belt buckle may not properly restrain a passenger during a crash. Dealers will inspect the second-row outer seat belt lower anchor bolts and repair or replace them as necessary, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ford and Lincoln Rearview Camera Image May Invert
item.description: The image on the center display may flip or turn upside down, showing an incorrect rearview image when the vehicle is put into reverse. Because the rearview image is not displayed correctly, these vehicles do not meet federal safety standards for rear visibility. To fix the problem, Ford dealers will update the software in the accessory protocol interface module at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Wiper Motor May Fail To Work
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer, Escape, Lincoln Aviator, and Lincoln Corsair vehicles because the windshield wiper motor may fail. If the motor fails, the windshield wipers may stop working properly, which can make it harder for the driver to see the road. Dealers will inspect the front wiper motors and replace them if necessary, at no cost to the owner. A final repair is expected to be available in October 2026.

item.title: Ford Explorer, Mustang, Nautilus EGR Valve Failure
item.description: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve in your vehicle may fail. If that happens, you could unexpectedly lose drive power while you're driving down the road. Dealers will replace the EGR valve, free of charge. Owner notification letters have already been mailed to affected owners.

item.title: Ford and Lincoln Trailer Brake and Light Failure
item.description: When towing a trailer, the integrated trailer module in certain Ford and Lincoln vehicles may lose communication with the vehicle. This can cause a loss of trailer brake and turn signal lights, or a loss of trailer brake function.

item.title: Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair Hybrid Battery Defect
item.description: On these Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair plug-in hybrid vehicles, a manufacturing defect in one or more high voltage battery cells may cause an internal short circuit and battery failure.

item.title: Ford Expedition, Lincoln Navigator Brake Assist Can Fail
item.description: On affected vehicles, the module that provides power assist for the brakes can malfunction while you are driving, or while a driver-assist feature is active. When this happens, the vehicle loses power brake assist. If it happens while a driver-assist feature is engaged, the vehicle may not brake the way you expect.

item.title: Lincoln MKT B-Pillar Door Trim Can Detach
item.description: On affected Lincoln MKT vehicles, the trim panel covering the pillar next to the driver's and front passenger's doors can come loose and detach while you are driving. Because this happens while the vehicle is in motion, a piece of trim landing on the road can become a hazard for you and other drivers nearby. Ford has already mailed an interim letter about this safety risk, with a full repair notice to follow once the fix is ready.

item.title: Lincoln Navigator reverse lights may flicker or fail
item.description: On certain 2025 Lincoln Navigator vehicles, the light bar across the back may have cracks in its outer lens or in a weld, letting moisture build up inside. That moisture can make the reverse lights flicker or stop working altogether. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for lamps and reflectors. Dealers will replace the rear light bar. Owner notification letters were mailed in January 2026.

item.title: Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair plug-in hybrid battery may fail
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair plug-in hybrid vehicles. One or more of the cells inside the high voltage battery may have been built with a defect. That defect can cause a short circuit inside the battery, and the battery can then fail. Dealers will update two control units, the ones that manage the battery and the hybrid system. Vehicles fixed under an earlier recall still need this new repair done.

item.title: Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator Windshield Bubbles
item.description: Certain Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles have windshields with visible air bubbles in the glass. These bubbles can block or blur part of the driver's view out of the windshield.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Moonroof Wind Deflector May Detach
item.description: On some Ford Expedition, F-150, F-250, F-350, F-450, and Lincoln Navigator vehicles, the clips holding the moonroof wind deflector may not be attached properly. This can allow the wind deflector to come loose and detach from the vehicle while driving. Dealers will inspect the moonroof wind deflector and repair it as necessary, at no cost to you. A detached wind deflector could become a hazard on the road for other drivers.

item.title: Ford and Lincoln rearview cameras may show blank image
item.description: Ford is recalling a range of Ford and Lincoln vehicles, including the Fiesta, Flex, Explorer, Escape, C-Max, Fusion, Taurus, Mustang and the Lincoln MKT and MKZ. On these vehicles, the camera that shows what is behind you when you shift into reverse may show a picture that is distorted, that cuts in and out, or that is blank. Ford says dealers will check the camera and replace it if needed.

item.title: Ford Explorer, Lincoln Aviator Have Loose Hitch Bolts
item.description: On some Explorer and Aviator SUVs, the bolts holding the trailer hitch in place may not be tight enough. If you are towing a trailer, loose hitch bolts can make the vehicle harder to control, and in some cases the trailer could come loose and detach from the vehicle. Either of these problems raises the chance of a crash while towing.

item.title: Lincoln Corsair Rear Lights May Fail From Water
item.description: Water may leak into the left and right rear combination light assemblies on some Corsair SUVs. This can cause the reverse light, tail light, brake light, or rear turn signal to stop working.

item.title: Ford and Lincoln Block Heater Fire Risk
item.description: In certain Ford and Lincoln vehicles, the engine block heater can crack and develop a coolant leak. If the block heater is plugged in when this happens, it can short circuit.

item.title: Ford Expedition, Lincoln Navigator Battery Fire Risk
item.description: A short circuit inside the battery junction box on some Expedition and Navigator vehicles can cause a fire in the engine. This can happen whether the vehicle is being driven or is sitting parked. Ford dealers will inspect the battery junction box and replace it if needed, remove a related ground wire, and on some vehicles install an extra electrical box with a connecting wire, all free of charge.

item.title: Ford Rearview Camera May Show Distorted Image
item.description: Some Ford pickup trucks, SUVs, vans, and the Lincoln MKC may have a problem with the rearview camera. When the vehicle is shifted into reverse, the camera image on the screen may appear distorted, show an upside-down picture, or go completely blank instead of a normal picture. Because of this, the driver may not have a clear view of what is behind the vehicle while backing up.

item.title: Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator Trailer Lights May Fail
item.description: Some Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles have a body control module that was not manufactured correctly. When you tow a trailer, this problem can cause the trailer's tail lights to fail to turn on the way they should. Because these lights are not working properly, the vehicle does not meet federal safety standards for lights and reflective equipment. This mainly affects visibility for the trailer being towed behind the vehicle.

item.title: Ford Edge Lincoln MKX Rear Brake Hose May Leak
item.description: On certain Edge and MKX vehicles, the rear brake jounce hose may rupture and leak brake fluid.

item.title: Lincoln Corsair Rearview Camera Display Problem
item.description: On certain 2020-2022 Lincoln Corsair vehicles, water may get into the rearview camera's connectors. This can cause the rearview camera image to not show up on the display, or to appear distorted.

item.title: Ford Mustang, Lincoln Nautilus Headlights May Fail
item.description: Some Lincoln Nautilus, Mustang Mach-E, and Mustang vehicles have LED driver modules that may contain a burnt diode. This can cause the low-beam and high-beam headlights, daytime running lights, front position lights, and front turn signals on the affected side to stop working. On Nautilus vehicles, it may also cause the rear tail light, rear turn signal, and rear position light to stop working.

item.title: Lincoln Nautilus Power Windows May Pinch Occupants
item.description: Certain Lincoln Nautilus vehicles that were previously repaired under an earlier recall still have a problem with the power window safety feature. The system that is supposed to stop a window and reverse it when it senses an obstruction may not work correctly.

item.title: Ford Expedition, Lincoln Navigator Lose Brake Assist
item.description: The electronic brake booster, which helps power the brakes, may malfunction while you're driving. This can happen on its own or while a driver-assist feature is active. If it malfunctions, you lose power assistance for braking, meaning it takes more effort and more distance to stop the vehicle. This can also affect how the vehicle brakes when driver-assist features are controlling it.

item.title: Lincoln Aviator Power Windows May Not Reverse
item.description: Some 2025 Lincoln Aviator vehicles have rear side windows that may not work correctly with the automatic closing feature. When one of these windows is closing and encounters an object in its path, it may exert too much force before automatically reversing direction. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety requirement for how power windows are supposed to behave when they meet resistance while closing.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln fuel pump may fail, stall engine
item.description: On certain Ford and Lincoln models, the low-pressure fuel pump may fail. If it fails, the engine can stall while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Ford Expedition, Lincoln Navigator Airbag Force Defect
item.description: Ford is recalling certain 2025 Lincoln Navigator and Ford Expedition vehicles. The passenger side air bag installed on these vehicles may have been manufactured incorrectly. Because of this manufacturing error, the air bag can deploy with excessive force if it goes off during a crash.

item.title: Ford and Lincoln rearview cameras may show blank image
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Ford and Lincoln vehicles, including the Explorer, Escape, F-150, Expedition, Ranger, Mustang, Bronco Sport, Maverick, Transit and the Lincoln Aviator, Corsair, Navigator and Nautilus. A software problem can make the rearview camera show a blank picture when the vehicle is backing up. The picture can also stay on the screen after the driver has finished backing up. Dealers will update the rearview camera software at no cost. Letters were mailed to owners in September 2025.

item.title: Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator second-row seats may move
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles. The switch for the easy-entry second-row outer seats can bind or stick. When that happens, the seat can unlatch, fold, or slide on its own while the vehicle is being driven. Dealers will inspect the switch and replace the trim piece around it if needed, at no cost. Ford has mailed notification letters to owners, and a customer service number is available for questions.

item.title: Lincoln Navigator Headlight Software May Cause Lights To Fail
item.description: In some Lincoln Navigator vehicles, the computer software that controls the headlights may cause the side marker lights and the daytime running lights to stop working. These lights help other drivers see your vehicle on the road. If they fail, the vehicle becomes less visible to other drivers, which can make it easier for a crash to happen. This is affecting vehicles that were already repaired once before under an earlier recall for a similar headlight problem.

item.title: Lincoln Aviator rear trim pieces may come loose
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Lincoln Aviator SUVs. The bars that divide the rear door windows and the trim on the pillar behind the rear doors may not have enough adhesive holding them in place. Without enough bonding, those pieces can come away from the vehicle. Dealers will repair or replace the pillar appliques and the window division bars on the vehicles that are covered by this recall.

item.title: Ford Escape, Maverick, Lincoln Corsair Engine Fire Risk
item.description: Certain Ford Escape, Lincoln Corsair, and Ford Maverick hybrid and plug-in hybrid vehicles were repaired incorrectly under an earlier recall. If the engine fails, engine oil and fuel vapor may be released into the engine compartment and build up near hot engine or exhaust parts, which are possible sources of ignition. This may result in a fire in the engine compartment.
